summary.headline: Bajaj Finance Q4 FY26: AUM crossed INR 5 lakh crore (up 22.4% YoY), PAT up 26.7%, and FY27 credit cost guided lower at 1.45%-1.60%.
summary.overview: Management reported a strong Q4 FY26 on core metrics: AUM reached about INR 510,000 crore (up 22.4% YoY), PAT grew 26.7% and PBT 26%, before one-time items. A revised presentation moved recoveries on written-off loans into loan losses, lowering loan loss to average AR to 1.65% from 1.75% and raising opex to NTI to 33.8% from 33.2%, with no PBT or PAT impact. Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 20-24%, 15-17 million new customers, opex to NTI down 25-40 bps, ROA of 4.4-4.6% and ROE of 19-20%. The call was heavily framed around geopolitical contingency, AI transformation and a "cruise mode" posture after an aggressive post-COVID period.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM grew 115% and is about 3.5% of AUM (approx. INR 18,000 crore); management expects it to exceed 5% of AUM by FY27 and is doubling down on branch expansion.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Grew only 6% in FY26 (vs 25-30% earlier) after proactive risk cuts since Q2 FY26; monthly origination cut from about INR 1,800 crore to INR 1,400 crore. Management expects return to double-digit growth between Q2 and Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Captive 2W/3W (auto-finance)
segments.commentary: Now under 1% of AUM but 13% of Q4 GNPA and 5% of Q4 credit cost; attrition of about 60% (about INR 6,500 crore) in FY26, with book to wind down to under INR 1,500 crore by September 2026.

segments.name: Bajaj Housing Finance (BHFL)
segments.commentary: Disbursements and AUM up 23%, record loan approvals up 37%, opex to NTI 19.2% (vs 21.8%), GNPA 27 bps and NNPA 11 bps; PAT ex one-time reversals up 20%.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Securities (BFSL)
segments.commentary: AUM up 77%, profit up 50%, ROE 10.5%, and 124,000 new customers added in Q4.

segments.name: Business and professional loans
segments.commentary: Only portfolio still showing yellow on asset quality; management expects it to turn green as the denominator grows from Q2 or Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of 20-24% (CFO also referenced 22-24% in answers), assumed contingent on easing geopolitical tensions and macro stability.
FY27 credit cost (loan loss to average AR, revised basis) of 1.45-1.60%, down from 1.75% in FY26 on the old basis; guidance excludes any adverse geopolitical impact.
NIM expected to moderate marginally, contingent on interest rate path.
Opex to NTI to improve by a further 25-40 bps from current levels.
ROA guidance 4.4-4.6% for FY27 (Q4 FY26 at 4.6%); ROE guidance 19-20% (Q4 FY26 at 20%).
Add 15-17 million new customers in FY27; profit growth expected to exceed balance sheet growth; MSME to return to double-digit growth from Q2-Q3 FY27.
Long-term ROA 4.3-4.7% and ROE 20-22% reiterated; FY27 management expects 600-plus autonomous AI agents deployed.
capex_capacity: Company does not publish overall AI capex; management said it is 'not pulling back any stops' on investment.
AI unit at 203 people, expected to grow to about 363 by June 2027; 27 AI voice and text bots live, with all customer engagement moving to bot interface by June 2026.
Planned deployment of close to 2,700 cameras across 3,000 stores/branches for customer identification.
AI voice agents now 30% of outbound voice agents (from 5,000 outbound agents), with management citing one-third the cost of human agents.
Diwali peak processing capacity expected to rise to about 1 million loan accounts per day next year (vs 600,000 this year, against 100,000 without AI).
demand_pricing: Monthly loan bookings are tracking toward 5 million-plus, versus a previous peak of about 4.6 million during festive season; management said it has never done 5 million loans in a month.
Gold loan branch expansion accelerated; 50% of Q4 employee additions (just under 1,800) were in gold loans and MFI.
New businesses contributed about 3-3.5% of AUM growth in FY26; 2-wheeler (open architecture, 3 years old) sees 50% of customers as existing-to-franchise (ETV) customers.

Car finance: 43-45% of new car loan customers each month are ETV customers (INR 450-500 crore monthly volume). Personal loan market share 8.5-9%; 40-45% of personal loan takers in India come from the 120 million franchise.
Market share of total net credit in India rose from 225 bps to 250 bps with the INR 100,000 crore AUM addition; management aims to grow at 2x system credit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Does 145-160 bps credit cost guidance assume any geopolitical impact, and is the reconciliation from 1.75% to 1.65% correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst's bridge was confirmed: 165 bps in Q4 net provisions, FY26 175 bps going to 145-160 bps. Management said guidance excludes any adverse geopolitical impact, with some conservatism built in; CFO noted that the old 165-175 bps range converts to 145-170 bps on the new presentation.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 ROA of 4.4-4.6% dependent on NIM expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no NIM expansion is needed; ROA of 4.6% in FY26 core is the base, supported by 22-24% growth, opex to NTI improvement and lower loan loss to AR. Management cites 4 levers: growth, margin, opex and credit costs.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will grow faster than the overall book in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loans, tractors and CVs have low bases and are expected to outgrow; gold to reach around 5% of AUM. Captive 2W/3W attrition will ease and MSME should return to double-digit growth from H2 FY27. Portfolio mix to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is AI capex, ROI and P&L impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Company does not disclose AI capex. Benefits cited: AI voice agents at one-third the cost, faster processing, and FY27 seen as the busiest year for AI outcomes; 600-plus autonomous agents planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PCR so high and will it unwind next year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ECL is now a quarterly bottom-up exercise, PCR should stay in the current corridor, and management intends to keep building provisions for balance-sheet resilience.

qa_highlights.question: Will profit growth reach 35-40% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said profit growth may be faster than balance sheet growth but did not validate a 35% figure; management described tailwinds from credit cost and cost efficiency, subject to geopolitical stability.

qa_highlights.question: How does 20-24% AUM growth compare with the long-term 20%+ target?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the long-term commitment is 20%-plus per year. Management aims to grow at about 2x system credit growth, targeting a top 5-6 lender position within 5-7 years.

risks_watch: Geopolitical conflict (West Asia / Iran-US) and macro shocks; management says all guidance is contingent on easing tensions, and any adverse event could push credit cost above guidance.
MSME recovery timing: growth must return to double digits from Q2-Q3 FY27 after 6% growth in FY26.
NIM moderation linked to interest rate path; cost of funds at 7.41%.
Business and professional loans remain the only portfolio not yet improving on asset quality.
Opex pressure from Labour Code costs and accelerated gold loan branch expansion; AI investment spend not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core momentum and credit cost tailwinds, but explicitly conditional on geopolitical stability and macro conditions. Management was candid about the post-COVID boom-era decisions and says it is moving to a more calibrated 'cruise mode'. It was evasive on AI capex, P&L payback and the 35% profit growth question.
key_quotes: Headwind over headwind virtually would consume twice the fuel. Thankfully, we are entering the year with tailwinds.
We are not pulling back any stops in investing whatever it takes in being front of the seat and center.
So long -term commitment continues to remain to be anchored at 20% plus number '22, '23, '24.
And to summarize the point, you should see us from here on in a reasonable cruise mode.

adds.what: Gold loan branch expansion (accelerated; 50% of Q4 employee additions in gold loans and MFI)
Planned deployment of close to 2,700 cameras across 3,000 stores/branches for customer identification
AI unit headcount from 203 to about 363 by June 2027

growth.why: FY27 AUM growth guided at 20-24% (midpoint 22%), backed by record Q4 AUM addition of about INR 25,500 crore, 15-17 million new customers, and market share gains (225 to 250 bps), with pricing/cost levers (opex to NTI down 25-40 bps) but no specific new capacity or order book quantified; MSME recovery and AI-driven cost gains are partly backed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Credit cost falls to 1.45-1.60% from 1.75% and opex to NTI improves 25-40 bps from 33.8%, offsetting a marginal NIM moderation (cost of funds 7.41%), supporting ROA of 4.4-4.6% and ROE of 19-20%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gold loan AUM up 115% to about INR 18,000 crore (3.5% of AUM), management targets over 5% of AUM by FY27 and is accelerating branch expansion, with 50% of Q4 employee adds (just under 1,800) in gold loans and MFI; ~2,700 cameras planned across 3,000 stores/branches.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM growth guided 20-24% (midpoint 22%) after record Q4 AUM addition of about INR 25,500 crore; 15-17 million new customers planned vs 17.5 million in FY26, and monthly loan bookings tracking toward 5 million-plus vs prior peak of 4.6 million.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation or capacity constraint was cited; management does not publish AI capex and said it is moving to a calibrated 'cruise mode', so no fresh capex programme was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit cost guided down to 145-160 bps from 175 bps in FY26 (165 bps in Q4 on revised basis), and opex to NTI to improve a further 25-40 bps, so profit growth could beat balance sheet growth if geopolitics stay calm; management did not validate 35% profit growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance (AUM 20-24%, credit cost 145-160 bps, ROA 4.4-4.6%) explicitly excludes adverse geopolitical impact; any West Asia/Iran-US shock could push credit cost above guidance, and MSME must return to double-digit growth from Q2-Q3 FY27 after 6% growth in FY26.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Car finance (43-45% of new car loan customers are ETV customers, INR 450-500 crore monthly), 2-wheeler open architecture, tractors and CVs are growing from low bases; 600-plus autonomous AI agents planned in FY27.

rows.label: Diwali peak processing capacity to ~1 million loan accounts/day
rows.why: Capacity expected to rise from 600,000 per day this year (100,000 without AI), enabling monthly bookings of 5 million-plus versus prior peak of 4.6 million.

rows.label: MSME return to double-digit growth
rows.why: MSME grew only 6% in FY26 (vs 25-30% earlier) after risk cuts; monthly origination cut from about INR 1,800 crore to 1,400 crore, and management expects a return to double-digit growth between Q2 and Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Captive 2W/3W book wind-down
rows.why: Book attrition of about 60% (about INR 6,500 crore) in FY26 and wind-down to under INR 1,500 crore by September 2026; the segment is 13% of Q4 GNPA and 5% of Q4 credit cost, so it should ease credit cost.

tone.note: Management was confident on core momentum, the record Q4 AUM addition and credit cost tailwinds, but explicitly conditional on geopolitical stability; analysts pushed on the 1.75% to 1.65% reconciliation, whether ROA needs NIM expansion, and the 35% profit growth question, and management was evasive
